key_insight: Whole-genome sequencing in Latin American early-onset and familial Parkinson’s patients uncovered clinically relevant genetic variants that standard array or targeted testing could miss.
clinical_relevance: These findings support broader genomic screening in selected Parkinson’s patients to improve detection of monogenic causes and inherited risk, especially in underrepresented Latin American populations.
method: Short-read whole-genome sequencing was performed on 263 individuals with early-onset and/or family-history-positive Parkinson’s disease.
The cohort had no known pathogenic Parkinson’s variant on prior genotyping data.
Researchers screened seven Parkinson’s genes plus 21 genes linked to related parkinsonian disorders.
evidence_signal: Among analyzed participants, 4.7% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in primary or secondary Parkinson’s genes, 5.5% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic GBA1 variants for Gaucher disease, and 2.7% carried known GBA1 risk variants.
watch_item: The study is a selected subset of patients with prior negative genotyping, so results may not generalize to all Parkinson’s populations and require careful variant interpretation.
paper_title: Genomic Landscape of Early-Onset and Familial Latin American Parkinson's Patients
